act: 11 CFR 111.24 (Federal Election Commission civil monetary penalties)
acts: Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act of 1990, 28 USC 2461 note

en.title: eCFR shows $84,852 in 11 CFR 111.24(a)(2)(ii); the January 2025 rule replaced it with $87,056
en.summary: The Federal Election Commission's 2025 inflation adjustment (90 FR 210, FR Doc. 2024-31368) amends section 111.24 by replacing the amount in paragraph (a)(2)(ii) with $87,056. The eCFR still shows the earlier $84,852 in its versions as of 31 December 2025 and 20 October 2026: the amendment to this paragraph was not incorporated.
en.impact: Anyone reading the eCFR sees a maximum penalty for a knowing and willful violation under paragraph (a)(2)(ii) that is $2,204 lower than the rule sets. No penalty actually assessed on the eCFR figure is claimed.

quotes.source: Federal Election Commission, Civil Monetary Penalties Annual Inflation Adjustments, 90 FR 210 (3 January 2025), FR Doc. 2024-31368
quotes.text: 2. Section 111.24 is amended in each paragraph indicated in the left column by removing the number indicated in the middle column and adding in its place the number indicated in the right column:

quotes.text: (ii) Notwithstanding paragraph (a)(2)(i) of this section, in the case of a knowing and willful violation of 52 U.S.C. 30122,the civil penalty shall not be less than 300% of the amount of any contribution involved in the violation and shall not exceed the greater of $84,852 or 1,000% of the amount of any contribution involved in the violation.

summary.en: The Office of the Federal Register replied that the amendment to paragraph (a)(2)(ii) had not been incorporated and that it will publish a CFR correction in the Federal Register. The correction has not yet been published.
